landing.cmpSubtitle: Everything this industry hides, we turned into product features.
landing.cmpBad1: Post winning screenshots only. Losing calls quietly disappear.
landing.cmpGood1: The market scores every signal automatically. Full record kept: we never built a delete button.
landing.cmpBad2: Calls are just a direction: "Gold is going up, get in!"
landing.cmpGood2: Every signal ships with entry, stop, target and risk-reward: a complete, executable plan.
landing.cmpBad3: The win rate is whatever they claim. No way to verify it.
landing.cmpGood3: Scoring rules are published and hard-coded: TP first is a win, SL first is a loss, ambiguous cases count against us.
landing.cmpBad4: They want your deposit, then want you to follow "the master".

landing.shTitle: What you'll see after you sign in
landing.shSubtitle: Keep scrolling: the screen walks you through the full flow, from receiving a signal to reviewing the record.
landing.sh1Pain: "Entries on gut feel, exits on mood, stops on luck."
landing.sh1Title: Every signal is a complete trading plan
landing.sh1Desc: Not "gold is going up", but a full executable plan: entry, stop, target and risk-reward. The multi-timeframe engine runs around the clock, and every signal carries an expiry countdown. Expired means expired: no hindsight calls.
landing.sh2Pain: "Right direction, but hesitation cost the entry. Can't cut losers, can't hold winners."
landing.sh2Title: One click to execute. Fear never gets a vote
landing.sh2Desc: Slide to confirm and the order lands in your own MT5 with stop and target already locked in at fill time. After that, no willpower required. You were never short on judgment: just on a hand that doesn't shake.
landing.sh3Pain: "Day job, can't watch charts. Wake up and the profit turned into a loss."
landing.sh3Title: Auto position management: it stands guard while you sleep
landing.sh3Desc: Once profit reaches target distance, the stop moves itself to break-even. Trailing stops follow the market, partial take-profit banks on schedule (PRO). Faster and steadier than moving stops by hand, with zero emotion.
landing.sh4Pain: "Other services only show you the winners."
landing.sh4Title: Wins and losses, all on the record
landing.sh4Desc: Every signal's final verdict is public. Losses render in the same font size as wins. Audit us on a free account for as long as you like: if the record holds up, then we can talk.
landing.scrTrailOn: Trailing stop active. Partial take-profit armed. Rules are measured in R (initial risk) and only ever move in your favor.
landing.exTitle: Engineered for the worst case, even where you can't see it
landing.ex1Title: Position size from risk %, steady even for beginners
landing.ex1Desc: Tell it what percent of the account you're willing to risk and it sizes the lot from the stop distance. "Risk 1% per trade" goes from slogan to default setting.
landing.ex2Desc: Connection dropped? PC off? Any order unexecuted after 5 minutes voids itself. Nothing ever fills at a stale price behind your back.
landing.ex3Desc: Order status, fill price and position P&L stream back in real time. Every trade is reviewable and reconcilable, tracked like a parcel.
landing.wrTitle: The market scores our win rate. We don't
landing.wrSubtitle: After every signal fires, the system tracks the market and scores it by one published rulebook. No human filtering, no "that one doesn't count".
landing.wrRule1: Price hits take-profit first → scored as a WIN
landing.wrRule1Note: Based on actual market prices touched, independent of anyone's trading.
landing.wrRule2: Price hits stop-loss first → scored as a LOSS
landing.wrRule2Note: A loss is a loss. The record is permanent: nothing deleted, nothing hidden.
landing.wrRule3: Both touched inside one candle → conservatively scored as a LOSS
landing.wrRule3Note: When the order of events can't be known, we'd rather make our number look worse than guess in our own favor.
landing.wrRule4: Signals with a market-data outage → excluded from stats
landing.wrRule4Note: Neither a win nor a loss, so bad data never pollutes the win rate.
landing.wrNote: Register to see the live signal win rate plus your own real trading performance: two separate ledgers, neither one polished.

landing.howTitle: Three steps from signup to your first trade
landing.howSubtitle: About 5 minutes end to end. No coding required
landing.step1Desc: Register free and instantly see the signal panel, the history and the published scoring rules.
landing.step2Desc: Download the connector, paste your token, and your MT5 comes online. No account? Minutes to open, demo works too.
landing.step3Desc: Pick a signal, confirm the lot size, and the order lands in your MT5 with stop and target attached.
landing.faq1q: Is my money safe? Do you ever touch my funds?
landing.faq1a: No, and we couldn't. Your funds stay in an account opened in your own name at the partner broker; PRISMX never handles them. Our connector does exactly one thing: it sends the orders you have confirmed to the MT5 terminal running on your own machine. You can disconnect or reset your token at any time.
landing.faq2q: Is this an automated trading bot (EA)? Could it trade behind my back?
landing.faq2a: No. PRISMX makes no decisions for you: every single order requires your explicit confirmation before it is sent. What it solves is everything after the confirmation: position sizing, stop and target placement, execution speed and receipts.
landing.faq3q: Is the win rate real? What stops you from faking it?
landing.faq3a: No human touches the scoring. After a signal fires the system tracks the market: take-profit first is a win, stop-loss first is a loss, both-touched-in-one-candle counts against us, and data outages are excluded. Everyone sees the same number on the panel, and we can't edit it either.
landing.faq4q: I'm a complete beginner. Can I use this?
landing.faq4a: Yes. Beginners arguably benefit the most. You don't need to read charts or indicators: every signal carries a complete plan, and you can size positions simply as "the percent of my account I'm willing to risk". We recommend starting on a demo account.
landing.faq5q: What do I need to get connected?
landing.faq5a: Three things: 1) an MT5 account at the partner broker MakeCapital (live or demo, takes minutes to open); 2) a Windows PC running MT5 that stays on and online; 3) a PRISMX account. Your phone can watch signals and send orders from anywhere; execution happens on that PC's MT5.
landing.faq6a: We focus on gold (XAUUSD), major currency pairs, and popular instruments like BTC. Deliberately not "everything": going deep on a few instruments across timeframes beats spreading thin across a hundred.
landing.faq7q: Does it cost anything right now?
landing.faq7a: FREE is free forever (delayed signals plus the public record, built for auditing us). PRO is a subscription: see the pricing section on this page for current prices, yearly is better value, USDT accepted. Any price changes are announced in advance.
landing.faq8q: Will following the signals make me money?
landing.faq8a: Nobody can promise that, and anyone who does is lying to you. Trading always carries risk and past win rates never guarantee future results. What PRISMX provides is discipline and transparency: complete plans, locked-in stops, honest records. The decisions, and the risk, stay yours.
landing.faq9q: What's actually different between FREE and PRO?
landing.faq9a: One word: timing. FREE shows signals only after they expire (about a 10-minute delay), which makes it perfect for auditing the record and learning the plan structure, but structurally impossible to trade on. PRO is real-time delivery plus one-click execution, auto position management and your personal real win rate. FREE exists so you can audit us for free; upgrade only once the record has earned it.

landing.expEyebrow: What Signal Groups Won't Tell You
landing.expTitle: Every card that burns is a lie the industry tells
landing.expSubtitle: These tricks work — so we built a no-lie version of each one. Same effect, zero fraud.
landing.expDark1: Post only winning screenshots. Losing calls quietly disappear.
landing.expDark2: Calls are just a direction: "Gold is going up!" No stop-loss.
landing.expDark3: Win rate is whatever they claim. No way to verify.
landing.expDark4: They want your deposit, then you follow "the master."
landing.expDark5: When reputation burns, disband and relaunch under a new name.
landing.expDark6: Never teach the principles — so you can never leave them.
landing.expMirror1: The market scores every signal automatically. We never built a delete button — you can't delete, even if you wanted to.
landing.expMirror2: Every signal ships with entry, stop, target and risk-reward: a complete, executable plan.
landing.expMirror3: Scoring rules are published and hard-coded: TP first is a win, SL first is a loss, ambiguous cases count against us.
landing.expMirror4: Zero custody. Your money sits in your own broker account. We couldn't touch it if we tried.
landing.expMirror5: Our brand is chained to an unbroken daily public record. One missing day counts as a loss for us.
landing.expMirror6: We openly teach risk management principles (that builds trust), but never the signal logic (that's the moat). You'll learn discipline; you'll still need the execution system.
landing.expMirror7: Real caps, real deadlines. When the clock runs out, the price goes up. The first time we prove we mean it, you'll believe every limit we set after that.
landing.expNote: This isn't aimed at any specific service. It's the state of the industry — and the reason we built this product.
landing.plTitle: From generation to verdict: every signal travels this tunnel
landing.plFootnote: At the end of the pipe, a crystal ledger. Wins and losses engraved side by side, same font size.
landing.deTitle: Three pillars lock your stop-loss. Your only job is to execute the plan.
landing.deSubtitle: At open: stop is locked. At profit target: auto break-even. As it runs: trailing stop follows. You sleep, it guards.
landing.tdTitle: Pick the tier that fits you
landing.tdDoorADesc: $49/month unlocks all real-time signals and execution
landing.tdDoorBDesc: Deposit $500+ and keep trading. PRO is sponsored by the broker — your money stays in your own account.
landing.tdFootnote: Door A: money spent. Door B: money still there. Both doors lead to PRO — we just got the broker to cover your tab.
landing.plStep1Desc: Our engine produces signals with five key elements: instrument, direction, entry, stop-loss, and take-profit. Each signal is a complete, executable plan.
landing.plStep2Desc: Review the signal in your PRISMX panel, then send it to your own broker's MT5 with one click. Your funds stay in your account — we never touch them.
landing.plStep3Desc: The market scores every trade. TP first = win, SL first = loss, edge cases count against us. Every result is engraved in the public ledger — no delete button exists.
landing.dc1: The moment you open, the stop is written and locked. You can't override it — that is discipline.
landing.dc2: When floating profit hits the threshold, stop moves to break-even. From that moment on, this trade can never lose.
landing.dc3: As profit runs, stop trails the market automatically. You don't need to watch the screen — sleep is safe.
landing.footerRisk: Risk warning: trading forex, precious metals and crypto assets carries a high level of risk and may result in the loss of your capital. Past signal performance does not guarantee future results. PRISMX provides technical signals and execution tooling only and does not constitute investment advice; whether and how to trade remains entirely your decision.

winrate.title: Win Rate by Session
winrate.hint: Covers TradingView platform signals only, pinned to the last 7 days, filed by the session they fired in. Win rate = take-profits / (take-profits + stop-losses); signals with no outcome yet or with broken price tracking stay out of the denominator. Sessions are defined in each centre's local time, so DST changeovers are followed automatically. The European and New York sessions overlap by about four hours daily and signals in the overlap count toward both, so the per-session samples add up to more than the total.
winrate.empty: No TradingView signals in this window.
winrate.thinSampleHint: {{resolved}} resolved out of {{samples}} signals — too few for a percentage.
winrate.footnote: Cells with fewer than {{min}} resolved trades show the count instead of a percentage: turning three or four results into a percentage looks like a conclusion but is indistinguishable from a coin flip.
winrate.recoEmpty: Data accumulates since 2026-08-21; {{resolved}} resolved so far. Combos appear here once they reach {{min}}.
winrate.recoStalled: Resolution is stalled (see the health bar above); recommendations are paused — recommending on stale data would be lying.

chart.sessionsHint: Filed by the session a signal fired in. The European and New York sessions overlap ~4h daily and signals in the overlap count toward both.
chart.sidesHint: Legacy signals with an unrecognized direction count toward neither side, so the two may sum to less than the total.
chart.holdingHint: Average time from a signal firing to reaching take-profit or stop-loss; resolved signals only.
chart.weekdayHint: Pinned to the last 7 days: a rolling 168 hours is exactly 7x24, so every weekday draws exactly 24 hours and the cells are directly comparable. Read across to compare weekdays, down to compare directions. Resolved signals only — anything without an outcome is excluded; each cell gates on its own 5-trade minimum and shows the raw count below it. Weekdays are UTC.

discipline.helpTitle: How is the discipline score calculated?
discipline.helpIntro: This score only looks at whether you followed the plan — it has nothing to do with whether the trade made money. The total is a weighted average of the three checks below (stop-loss 40%, position size 30%, exit 30%).
discipline.helpStopBody: Checks whether you undid the signal's stop-loss — opening without a stop, moving the stop in the losing direction, or removing it entirely all count as a violation. The system's own automatic adjustments (break-even, trailing stop) don't count against you.
discipline.helpVolumeBody: Checks whether this trade's size is much bigger than what you normally place (over 3x). A sudden jump in size is often a "revenge trade" trying to win back a loss — flagged as a violation.
discipline.helpExitBody: Checks whether you manually closed a position before it hit its stop-loss or take-profit. Closing at a loss counts as a violation (likely a panic exit); closing at a profit doesn't.
discipline.helpNote: Only counts orders placed against a signal, and only actions taken through the website — anything done directly in the MT5 terminal isn't visible to the system and is treated as compliant.

strategy.templateBollingerBreakoutDesc: Buy when the close breaks above the upper band, sell when it breaks below the lower band — betting on breakout continuation.

faqPage.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqPage.intro: Everything about fund safety, requirements, signal scoring and subscriptions. The first 9 match the homepage FAQ; the rest go deeper.
faqPage.q10: Is it MT5 only? Can I use MT4?
faqPage.a10: MT5 only for now. One-tap execution and automatic position management rely on MT5's integration capabilities, which MT4 cannot match — and accounts at the partner broker are MT5 by default.
faqPage.q11: My PC can't stay on all day. Can I use a VPS?
faqPage.a11: Yes. Any Windows environment that runs MT5 can play the execution role, including a cloud Windows VPS. A common setup is exactly that: MT5 on a VPS stays online while your phone watches signals and sends orders.
faqPage.q12: What happens when PRO expires or I stop paying?
faqPage.a12: You simply drop back to FREE. Your account, history and personal win rate are all kept — nothing is deleted, and you can upgrade again anytime. USDT payments have no auto-renewal: the panel reminds you before expiry, and not paying just means not being charged.
faqPage.q13: Why do I have to use the partner broker's MT5 account?
faqPage.a13: Because the win-rate scoring must reconcile with your actual fills. Signals are scored, priced and executed against one quote source; a different broker's spread and pricing quirks would open a gap of "the record won but my account didn't". Locking one quote source is what makes the public record auditable.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of Signal Lab (the "Service"). By registering an account or otherwise using the Service, you confirm that you have read and accept these terms. If you do not accept them, please do not register or use the Service.

sections.h: What the Service is, and what it isn't
p: The Service is a trading-signal and execution toolkit: we show you signals produced by technical indicators, and provide a local bridge app that forwards your confirmed instructions to your own MT5 terminal.

The Service is not an advisory service and does not constitute investment advice, an offer, or a solicitation. We do not decide for you, do not trade on your behalf, and never touch or custody your funds — your money stays in your own broker account at all times.
Whether to trade, what to trade and at what size are entirely your decisions, and the consequences are entirely yours. The Service makes no promise or guarantee about any trading outcome.
You register with a valid email address, or sign in with Google. An account is for one person and may not be transferred, rented out or shared.

You are responsible for safeguarding your password and your API token. The API token is equivalent to a password: anyone holding it can send trading instructions to your MT5 account. If you suspect it has leaked, reset it immediately on the Connect MT5 page.
Any action taken through your account or API token is treated as taken by you.
The Service has two tiers, FREE and PRO. FREE costs nothing; PRO is a monthly or yearly subscription at the prices shown on the upgrade page.

PRO is paid in cryptocurrency (USDT). Please note that a blockchain transfer is irreversible once confirmed — we cannot reverse a completed transfer for you. Refunds are therefore not offered as a rule; if the Service is unavailable for an extended period through our fault, contact us and we will handle it case by case.

Subscriptions do not auto-renew and nothing is auto-charged. On expiry your tier automatically returns to FREE, and real-time signals, push notifications and any MT5 connections beyond the FREE limit stop with it. To continue, renew manually before the expiry date.

A free trial, where offered, may be claimed once per account for life. If you convert to a paid subscription during a trial, the paid period starts from the moment of payment and does not stack on top of the remaining trial days.

You may not resell, rebroadcast or otherwise distribute the signals provided by the Service to third parties; reverse-engineer, mass-scrape or load-test the Service; attempt to bypass tier limits, rate limits or billing; or upload malicious content or interfere with other users.
We may suspend or terminate an account on discovering such behaviour, and paid but unused subscription time is not refunded in that case.
The Service depends on several third parties: your MT5 broker (trade execution), TradingView (signal source), NOWPayments (payments), Google (optional sign-in), and browser vendors' push services.

Each has its own terms and policies, independent of these terms, and we are not responsible for their availability, execution quality or conduct. In particular, your final fill price, spread, slippage and any rejection are entirely determined by your broker.

We make reasonable efforts to keep the Service available but do not promise 100% uptime. Maintenance, upgrades, upstream market-data outages, network failures and broker-side issues can all cause short periods of unavailability or delayed data.

The local bridge app requires your own computer to stay powered on, online and logged into MT5. No instruction can execute while the bridge is offline; any instruction not executed within 5 minutes is voided automatically so it can never fill later at a stale price.
To the maximum extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any trading loss, lost profit, lost opportunity or indirect loss arising from your use of, or inability to use, the Service.
Whatever the cause of action, our total aggregate liability to you is capped at the subscription fees you actually paid us in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
Nothing here excludes or limits liability that cannot be excluded by law.

We may update these terms from time to time. Substantive changes will be reflected in the "Last updated" date on this page and, where reasonable, flagged in the app. Continuing to use the Service after a change means you accept the new terms.
You may stop using the Service at any time and may contact us to delete your account. We may also terminate your account for a serious breach of these terms.
The limitation-of-liability section survives termination.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what information Signal Lab collects, why, where it is stored, who it is shared with, and what rights you have over your own data. Our principle is simple: collect only what running the service genuinely requires, and store nothing we can avoid storing.

p: Account data: your email address; when signing in with Google, also the account identifier and email-verification status Google returns. Passwords are stored as an irreversible hash — we cannot read your original password.
MT5 connection data: the login number, broker server name, account name, currency, balance, equity, leverage and symbol suffix reported by the bridge app, plus its online heartbeat time.

Trading records: the place / close / modify instructions you send through the platform and their receipts; and the real closing-deal records for platform-opened positions reported by the bridge (time, symbol, side, volume, fill price, P&L).

Usage statistics: page-view counts and dwell time (aggregated per page-and-hour, containing no user identity), plus a per-day dedup marker for "this user opened this page on this day" (day granularity only — no timestamp, no duration).

Technical data: your push subscription endpoint (when notifications are on), the bridge app's version, and request IP addresses (used only for rate limiting and failed-login lockout, never for profiling).
We never obtain — and technically cannot obtain — your MT5 trading account password. The bridge app reads terminals you have already logged into on your own computer.
We never touch or custody any of your funds.
We do not collect identity documents, bank card numbers or postal addresses. Crypto payments are handled by NOWPayments; we retain only the payment id, amount, currency and status.

We do not sell your personal data, nor trade it for any third party's marketing resources. Your browser's local storage holds only your login token and interface preferences (language, chart settings, selected tab).
To run the Service: showing signals, routing instructions to the correct MT5 account, computing your personal win rate and discipline score.
Security and abuse prevention: rate limiting, blocking credential stuffing, spotting anomalous activity, enforcing tier permissions.
Billing: confirming subscription status and expiry.

Product improvement: understanding which pages get used and for how long. This data is deliberately split so that we can answer "how many people opened the chart page on Tuesday" but cannot answer "when did this person look, and for how long".
The database is hosted on Supabase (PostgreSQL, Singapore region). The backend runs on a cloud server; the frontend is hosted and delivered by Vercel.
All traffic between clients and servers is encrypted in transit over HTTPS/WSS.

Because the Service is distributed across the regions above, your data may be transferred outside your own country and stored and processed there. By using the Service you acknowledge and agree to this.
We do not sell your personal data and do not trade it with anyone for marketing.

To operate, necessary data reaches these providers: Google (only if you use Google sign-in, to verify your identity), NOWPayments (payment processing), browser vendors' push services such as Google / Apple / Mozilla (only when notifications are on, to deliver them), and the cloud and database providers named above.

Advertising measurement: this site loads the Meta Pixel (Facebook advertising pixel). It stores cookies such as `_fbp` in your browser and reports which pages of this site you visited back to Meta, so we can measure ad performance and show retargeted ads. It cannot read your MT5 account, positions, trade history or payment details. You can limit this tracking through your browser's cookie settings, an ad blocker, or the Ad Preferences section of your Meta account.
We may disclose information where legally required, or where necessary to protect the Service and its users' legitimate interests.

Account and trading records are kept for as long as your account exists. Unbinding an MT5 account does not delete its historical fills — they simply stop counting toward your statistics, and re-binding restores the view.
Per-day page-visit dedup markers are pruned automatically after roughly 100 days.
1-minute candles are kept for 30 days by default; other timeframes are kept long-term (this is market data and contains no personal identity).
After you close your account we delete or anonymise your personal data within a reasonable period, except where the law requires retention.
You have the right to ask what personal data we hold about you, to have inaccurate information corrected, and to have your account and associated data deleted.
At any time you can turn notifications off on the account page, reset your API token on the Connect MT5 page, and review every trading record on the orders page.
To exercise any of these rights, get in touch with us. To protect your account we may need to verify your identity first.
The Service is not intended for anyone under 18. If we learn that we have unknowingly collected a minor's information, we will delete it promptly.
When this policy is updated we change the "Last updated" date on this page. Updates that substantively change how data is used will also be flagged in the app.

risk.title: Risk Disclosure
risk.intro: Please read this page carefully before using the Service. Trading forex, precious metals, oil and crypto assets is high risk and can cost you your entire capital — and under some leverage conditions, more than your capital. If you cannot afford that loss, do not trade.

sections.h: Leverage magnifies losses as well as gains
p: MT5 margin trading uses leverage, meaning a small price move can affect your account far out of proportion to your capital. Leverage amplifies profits and amplifies losses equally.
In violent moves, gaps or thin liquidity, a stop-loss may not fill at the price you set, and your actual loss can exceed what you expected.

sections.h: The Service is not investment advice
p: The signals shown are the automatic output of technical indicators applied to preset rules. They are not tailored to anyone's financial situation, investment objectives or risk tolerance, and therefore do not constitute — and must not be read as — investment advice or a recommendation.
We are not licensed investment advisers and offer no discretionary or managed-account service. Every trading decision is yours.

sections.h: Past performance does not predict future results
p: Every win rate, risk-reward ratio, equity curve, maximum drawdown and losing streak shown in the app is a statistic computed over historical data. None of it is a forecast or a promise of future returns.

Any stretch of history can contain luck, the more so the smaller the sample. That is why we withhold percentages until enough trades have resolved — a "100% win rate" derived from two or three trades is misleading, not informative.

Custom-strategy backtests do account for trading costs: entry pays half a spread plus one slippage in the direction of the trade, hitting a stop pays one further slippage penalty, and commission is charged once per round trip. These parameters are configured per symbol by the platform and may differ from the conditions at your own broker, so it is worth checking them against your account.

Backtests do not account for overnight swap, and do not simulate requotes, rejections or execution latency, nor can they reconstruct the order-book depth of the time. Some divergence between live results and backtest results is therefore normal, and a backtest is best treated as a reference point rather than an expectation of live performance.

Backtests run on the candle history this platform has accumulated, whose depth grows over time. Where data is insufficient or has gaps, the page states the range actually available — it is worth noting that range before reading the result, as the number of days selected and the number of days available are not always the same.

sections.h: Risks inherent to the execution path
p: An instruction sent from the web app has to be relayed to MT5 by the bridge app running on your own machine. If the bridge is offline, your computer is disconnected or powered off, or MT5 is not logged in or has algorithmic trading disabled, the instruction cannot execute.

Any instruction still unexecuted after 5 minutes is voided automatically, so a stale instruction can never fill later at an outdated price — but this also means an order you believe you placed may not have filled. Always treat the receipt on the orders page as the truth.
Quotes shown on this platform come from a market-data feed and may differ slightly from your broker's. The final fill price is whatever your broker executes.
Trade only with money you can afford to lose entirely. We recommend running the whole workflow on a demo account first.
Confirm for yourself whether this kind of trading is legal where you live and whether it must be declared for tax.
If you are unsure about the risk of a particular trade, consult an independent licensed professional.
